title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short bookkeeping computation in a ring of divided-power (PD) series, written on the back of a reused sheet. The verso and the neighbouring pages are typescript pages 56–57 of SGA 7, Exposé IX, on Néron models and semistable reduction; that text is unrelated to the manuscript computation.

Setting. Take a two-variable PD series φ(X,Y) = X + Σ_{i,j≥1} f_ij X^{(i)} Y^{(j)}. Substitute X = X_0 and Y = T − X_0, a linear change of PD coordinates as one does when comparing the two projections on a PD-neighbourhood of the diagonal. The divided-power binomial formula gives (T−X_0)^{(j)} = Σ_{0≤k≤j} T^{(j−k)} (−X_0)^{(k)}. The page writes X_0^k, sloppily dropping the divided-power brackets on X_0.

The result is
X_0 + Σ_{i,j,k} f_ij T^{(j−k)} (−1)^k X_0^{(i)} X_0^{k},
with 0≤k≤j and i,j≥1.

Reindexing. Grothendieck sets ν = i+k, so i = ν−k ≥ 1, i.e. 0≤k≤ν−1. He sets δ = j−k ≥ 0. The condition j ≥ sup(k,1) becomes (k,δ)≠(0,0), i.e. k+δ≥1.

An intermediate line has the wrong index f_{ν,k+δ}. It is crossed out and replaced by the correct f_{ν−k,k+δ}.

The outcome is a series Σ_{ν≥1} a_{1,ν} X_0^ν, with
a_{1,ν} = Σ_{0≤k≤ν−1, δ≥0, k+δ≥1} (−1)^k f_{ν−k,k+δ} T^{(δ)}.
In the ν=1 term (k=0) the separate summand X_0 must be added.

This gives A_0 = X_0·(1 + Σ_{δ≥1} f_{1,δ} T^{(δ)}) + (terms of higher order in X_0). The leading coefficient a_{1,1} = 1 + (PD-nilpotent terms) is a unit.

Purpose. The evident aim is to show that the transformed series is again a PD 'coordinate' in X_0 with invertible linear coefficient. Such a series is then invertible under substitution, which is what one needs to compare PD-polynomial or PD-series coordinates. This is typical of proving that the PD de Rham complex, or a PD-envelope, is independent of the choice of coordinates.

The last line, 'φ(X_0)', marks the start of the next step: viewing the result as a series in the single variable X_0.
errors: The products X_0^{(i)}·X_0^k are written as X_0^{i+k}. In divided powers, X^{(i)}X^{(k)} = C(i+k,i) X^{(i+k)}, so binomial factors are suppressed. Alternatively the notation is deliberately ambiguous between ordinary and divided powers; as written it is imprecise.
T^{(δ)} is written as T^δ in the final displayed sum. This is a notational inconsistency with the other lines.
An intermediate line with the index error f_{ν,k+δ} is crossed out and replaced by the correct f_{ν−k,k+δ}; the final formula is correct.

ideas.what: Reindexing a substituted two-variable PD series after a linear change of variables Y = T − X, extracting the coefficient of X_0^ν and checking that the linear coefficient is a unit
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power binomial formula / change of coordinates in PD-polynomial algebras (crystalline cohomology, PD de Rham complex)
ideas.where_published: Background of the 1968 Crystals notes; developed in Berthelot's 'Cohomologie cristalline' (1974)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine index-shuffling computation with divided powers, a scratch step toward coordinate invariance. Nothing new or uncredited appears. The only curiosity is that it is written on the back of an SGA 7 IX typescript sheet.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the factor should read X_0^{(i)} with divided-power brackets, as in the image.
In the final formula the index is f_{ν−k,k+δ}; the crossed-out line has f_{ν,k+δ}.
'(k=0, ν=1)' refers to the term giving a_{1,1}. The image reads '(k=0, ν=1)', consistent with the transcription.
The crossed-out fragment at the bottom is 'φ(ξ_1' or similar, preceding 'φ(X_0)'.
